acceptanceCriteria.rule: every adjacent bridge query must return raw values for BOTH anchors strictly above resolutionFloor; a bridge where either side rounds to <=0.5 is rejected and the ladder must add an intermediate rung instead of accepting a low-resolution bridge
acceptanceCriteria.stabilityRule: identical repeated query (same terms, same timeframe, same geo, short interval) must return identical or near-identical raw values before a bridge is accepted as reliable
acceptanceCriteria.minimumRungCount: smallest chain such that every adjacent pair clears resolutionFloor; not fixed in advance
acceptanceCriteria.noCohortDependency: anchor identities and bridge ratios are fixed constants, never derived from the currently eligible Pokemon population or from Collector Appeal set-ranking outcomes

chainErrorTest.description: Stunky's global value recovered via its properly-assigned Torkoal-rung bridge vs. via a deliberately mismatched direct Lucario pairing (Stunky+Lucario, a coarser/too-distant rung)
chainErrorTest.interpretation: proper rung assignment matters (raw target value degraded from 17.09 on the correct Torkoal-paired scale to 1.25 when paired with the much larger Lucario), but the calibration math tolerates a moderately mismatched pairing gracefully -- a 2.0% chain-error bound observed on this sample, not a catastrophic failure. This is one data point, not a full error-propagation study across the ladder.

stratifiedZeroSampleTest.description: Seedot, a previously-untested low-tier Pokemon, queried against its nearest assigned rung (Purugly) rather than the universal Pikachu anchor
stratifiedZeroSampleTest.interpretation: resolves clearly (well above the 0.5 floor on both sides) when paired with a magnitude-appropriate anchor -- consistent with the Stunky/Purugly findings from the prior session (both were 0.0/0.03 against Pikachu, both fully resolvable against peers)

mismatchedTierDegradationTest.description: Stunky (true local value ~17 on the Torkoal scale) queried directly against Lucario (a too-distant rung)
mismatchedTierDegradationTest.interpretation: confirms degradation is a continuum, not purely binary zero/nonzero: an improperly-tiered pairing does not always collapse fully to 0, but it does materially compress resolution (17.09 -> 1.25, a >13x reduction in representable precision) -- this is why nearest-rung assignment is required, not merely 'avoid the worst offender' (Pikachu).

knownLimitations.singleTemporalWindow: all bridge observations were captured within one short live session (today 1-m timeframe, single calendar day); true multi-week temporal stability (Phase 4's 'repeated-window' requirement in the fullest sense) has NOT been validated -- only same-session repeat-call determinism was tested (2 of 5 bridges repeat-checked, both identical). A production rollout should re-verify these bridge ratios at least once across a separate calendar week before treating them as long-term stable.
knownLimitations.sampleSize: anchor roster and diagnostics are based on 9 total live queries against a 6-anchor chain plus 2 stratified/diagnostic samples -- sufficient to validate the architecture and reject the prior universal-anchor design, but not a large-N statistical study.
knownLimitations.anchorSelectionMethod: anchor candidates (Purugly, Stunky, Torkoal, Lucario, Charizard, Pikachu) were chosen using general franchise-recognition tiering as an initial non-price hypothesis, then accepted/rejected purely on measured resolution -- consistent with the requirement that tier hints may only determine batching, never the final score.
